issue.title: [Bug] Claude Code 后台子代理的 <task-notification> 经 Magpie 后模型看不到（直连正常，A/B 可复现）
issue.body:
## 现象

Claude Code 经 Magpie 网关时，后台子代理（`Agent` 工具 `run_in_background: true`）完成后，客户端生成的 `<task-notification>` **模型看不到**；同一台机器、同一 Claude Code 版本直连 Anthropic 时能看到。表现为主会话“等不到子代理结果”，只能自己去读 output 文件。

## 环境

- Magpie 0.1.1290（macOS arm64，`redact` 开启）
- Claude Code 2.1.303
- 路由：`claude/claude-sonnet-5-5`（主）、`claude/claude-haiku-5-5`（子代理），served 均为 Anthropic 原生模型

## 复现（A/B，同一提示词）

探针提示词：

```text
1. Use the Agent tool with run_in_background: true and subagent_type "general-purpose". Its prompt: "Run the bash command `echo PROBE_7Q3X_DONE` and reply with only its output."
2. Immediately after launching it, run the Bash command `sleep 45` in the foreground.
3. After the sleep returns, do NOT read any output file, do NOT use TaskOutput, do NOT call any other tool.
4. Answer on one line: `SEEN <notification text>` if a completion notification for the background agent is visible to you, otherwise `NOT_SEEN`.
```

- 经 Magpie：`claude -p --setting-sources project --model claude/claude-sonnet-5-5 --output-format stream-json --verbose < probe.txt`（`ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` 指向 Magpie）
- 直连：同一命令，`env -u ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL -u ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN ...`，`--model claude-sonnet-5-5`，走 claude.ai 订阅登录（已核对该会话不在 Magpie routing 日志中）

| 路径 | 次数 | 结果 |
|---|---|---|
| 直连 | 2 | 2/2 `SEEN <task-notification>...` |
| 经 Magpie（含用户级设置） | 1 | `NOT_SEEN` |
| 经 Magpie（仅 project 设置，排除 hooks/插件） | 2 | 2/2 `NOT_SEEN` |

两边 stream-json 中客户端都发出了 `system/task_notification` 事件，且子代理都返回了 `PROBE_7Q3X_DONE`，差异只在网关。交互式会话中也多次复现（客户端 transcript 里通知以 `queued_command` 附件随下一次请求发出，但模型回复表明未看到）。

## routing 日志中的线索

`~/.config/magpie/routing/<date>.jsonl` 的 `prompt.parts` 分段统计（经 Magpie 的一次探针，主代理请求）：

```text
13:35:39 main  system=[environment 3388, prompt 2265]                 chat=290
13:36:30 main  system=[environment 3351, prompt 2241, harness 494]    results=[Agent 416, Bash 12]  chat=388
```

通知送达后的那次请求，`system` 段里**新出现一项 `harness`（≈494 tokens，与一条 task-notification 大小相当）**。交互式会话里也一样：通知到达那次请求的 `system.harness` 从 4251 跳到 4796（+545），相邻请求只变化个位数。

推测：Magpie 在改写请求时，把 user 消息里的 `<task-notification>` 当作 harness/系统注入文本识别出来，挪进了 system 段（或改变了形态），于是模型不再把它当作“刚到达的新事件”。这与 #1826（客户端插入的提醒被误判）可能是同一类问题。由于 routing 日志不含请求体，以上只能从分段统计推断，无法直接看到改写后的正文。

## 期望

`<task-notification>`（以及同类的后台任务事件）应保持在原来的 user 消息位置原样转发，不归入 system/harness。

## 临时绕过

主会话对后台任务改用阻塞等待 output 文件，不依赖完成通知。

comments.body:
## Summary

Through the Claude subscription bridge, a background task's `<task-notification>` never reaches the model. Claude Code sends the notification with the next request — the same one that carries the finished tools' results — and the bridge hands the waiting run the results plus only what it reads as the user's words. The notification falls through two filters built for the other tail notices and is dropped, so the model answers as if no task had ended: the main session "waits forever" on a subagent that finished. Direct connections show the notification; this reproduces with masking off, so `redact` is not a factor.

## Cause

The drop is in the Claude bridge's resume path, `saidWithResults` (internal/gateway/claude_subscription.go:3257):

1. Claude Code 2.1.296+ puts the texts that trail a turn's results — hooks' notices, the `<total_tokens>` count, a mid-turn user message — into one `{role: "system"}` message after the results (captured in #2060). A background task's `<task-notification>` travels the same way; the reporter's routing log shows it: a `harness` item of notification size appears in the request's `system` part exactly when the notification is due, beside `results=[Agent, Bash]` — the system message arriving with the results.
2. When the results answer calls a run is waiting on, the bridge resumes it with `continueWith` (internal/gateway/claude_subscription.go:3366): the tool results over MCP, plus `saidWithResults` queued first as a user message (`queue`, internal/gateway/claude_subscription.go:3424).
3. `saidWithResults` skips a system message outright (`case m.Role == "system" || m.Role == "developer"`, internal/gateway/claude_subscription.go:3273 — right for hook notices, #2060) and drops texts its `agentNotice` knows (internal/gateway/claude_subscription.go:3274) — and `agentNotice`'s injected leads include `"<task-notification>"` (internal/gateway/prompt.go:655), put there for turn reading, not delivery. Either shape of the notification — the system message, or the older client's user message of its own — is filtered out. The inner model is never told.
4. Every other path tells it: a run started anew is told the whole conversation, every message rendered (renderClaudePrompt, internal/gateway/claude_subscription.go:2598; renderClaudeTurn, internal/gateway/claude_subscription.go:2886), and a relayed request passes the body as sent. Only the run kept for the results — the common case of a foreground wait, as in the reporter's probe — loses it. That matches the A/B: 2/2 `SEEN` direct, 3/3 `NOT_SEEN` through magpie, with the client's own stream-json emitting the notification on both sides.

## Fix

`saidWithResults` now tells the run a text that carries the notification: a `taskNotice` case (a contains on `<task-notification>`) ahead of the system-message and `agentNotice` cases. Hooks' notices and token counts stay out — #2060's tests are unchanged and hold. The notification is queued to the run's Claude Code as its own message, so the model hears of the finished task the way it does on a request that carries the notification alone.

## Verification

| Check | Command | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Red on base | `go test ./internal/gateway/ -run TestClaudeTaskNotificationGoesOnWithTheResults -count=1` at `f5b01574` | FAIL, both shapes (below) |
| Directed, fixed | same `-run` plus the #2060 and turn tests, `-count=1 -v` | all pass |
| Ablation | fix reverted → red as on base; re-applied → green; `taskNotice` forced `false` → red; restored → green | as expected, each step |
| Race | `go test -race ./internal/gateway/ -run 'TestClaudeTaskNotificationGoesOnWithTheResults|TestClaudeHookNotices|TestClaudeUsersMessageAmongHookNoticesGoesOnAlone|TestTurnInSkipsWhatTheAgentPutIn|TestIntentHoldsPastWhatTheAgentPutIn' -count=1` | ok (2.148s) |
| Format, vet | `gofmt -l` on both touched files; `go vet ./internal/gateway/` | clean |
| Build | `go build ./...` on darwin/arm64; `GOOS=linux GOARCH=amd64 go build -tags nogui ./...`; `GOOS=windows GOARCH=amd64 go build ./...` | all ok |
| Full package | `go test ./internal/gateway/ -count=1 -p 1 -timeout 30m` | ok (320.989s) |

## Not verified

- End to end with a real Claude Code 2.1.303 against a Claude subscription: 2.1.303's exact notification bytes are inferred from #2060's captured 2.1.296 shapes and the reporter's routing-log segments, not captured here. The tests cover both known shapes (the system message, and the older user message).
- The direct-connection side (no magpie) is the reporter's A/B, not re-run here.

---

**Source**: reported in #3020 (WardLu, with an A/B probe and routing-log segments)

**Red without the fix** (base `f5b01574`):

```text
=== RUN   TestClaudeTaskNotificationGoesOnWithTheResults
=== RUN   TestClaudeTaskNotificationGoesOnWithTheResults/in_the_system_message
    claude_hook_notice_test.go:85: Claude Code was written [], want the task-notification
=== RUN   TestClaudeTaskNotificationGoesOnWithTheResults/a_message_of_its_own
    claude_hook_notice_test.go:85: Claude Code was written [], want the task-notification
--- FAIL: TestClaudeTaskNotificationGoesOnWithTheResults (0.00s)
    --- FAIL: TestClaudeTaskNotificationGoesOnWithTheResults/in_the_system_message (0.00s)
    --- FAIL: TestClaudeTaskNotificationGoesOnWithTheResults/a_message_of_its_own (0.00s)
FAIL
FAIL	github.com/yetone/magpie/internal/gateway	1.174s
```

**Siblings**: the gates live only in the Claude bridge — no other bridge reads `saidWithResults`/`agentNotice` (rg over internal/gateway: no consumers in the Codex, OpenCode or desktop subagent paths). The fresh-run prompt path writes the text either way (guard test `TestClaudePromptToldTheTaskNotification` passes on base too); `match` takes only tool results and images, unchanged; `parseAnthropicRequest`'s block-type switch drops unknown block types on translated routes only, and the notification rides in text blocks; `prompt.go`'s `injected` list is observation and turn detection, not delivery, and is untouched.

**When the read fails**: `taskNotice` is a contains on the text part, so a malformed or absent `<task-notification>` falls through to the unchanged filters — skipped as before, no new failure path. `queue`'s timeout path is untouched: if the run's Claude Code never acknowledges the queued message, the results still go on after 2s.

**Not verified**: end to end through a real bridge with a real Claude Code 2.1.303 and a real Claude subscription; the direct-connection side of the A/B.

Branch with the commit: [hunt57-c-task-notification](https://github.com/ggbdpq/magpie/tree/hunt57-c-task-notification) (head `d0a9ef61745d9d9900e26e7c32d05ecb7dacd303`).

**Attribution**: AI-written; the analysis, patch and tests were produced by a coding agent against the repository's own tests and fixtures, and every claim above carries the command that checked it. Please keep the author (`ggbdpq`) or add `Co-authored-by: ggbdpq <ggbdpq@gmail.com>`.

**Patch**: single commit on `f5b01574`, two files, +51/−0. SHA-256 first 16: `b61928472f034f1c`

Claude Code sends a background task's <task-notification> with the next
request: in the {role: "system"} message 2.1.296+ puts its other tail
notices in (#2060), or, older clients, as a text of its own. Through the
Claude subscription bridge, the run waiting on the request's tool results

a foreground wait on the task had nothing to wait for — the A/B of #3020:

the whole conversation, notification included; only the run kept for the
results lost it.

saidWithResults tells the run a text that carries the notification
(taskNotice, a contains on the tag) before the system-message and
agentNotice cases; hooks' notices and token counts stay out (#2060's

What changed:
- internal/gateway/claude_subscription.go: taskNotice, and a

- internal/gateway/claude_hook_notice_test.go: the notification goes on

- go test -race on the same -run: ok. gofmt -l on both files: clean.
  go vet ./internal/gateway: clean.
- go build ./... on darwin/arm64, GOOS=linux GOARCH=amd64 -tags nogui,
  GOOS=windows GOARCH=amd64: all ok.
- go test ./internal/gateway/ -count=1 -p 1 -timeout 30m: ok (320.989s).
- Not tried: end to end with a real Claude Code 2.1.303 on a Claude
  subscription. 2.1.303's exact notification bytes are inferred from
  #2060's captured 2.1.296 shapes and the reporter's routing log, not
  captured here.

Published a fix in my fork: https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/commit/b7726551109dae0bc6b406cb2dddd62abd9d4e2f

The Claude subscription resume path now preserves complete `<task-notification>` blocks that were previously discarded as injected agent/system/developer notices when returning tool results. Multiple notifications and notifications mixed with user text are covered. Hook payloads and token-count notices remain filtered; the queued-turn ordering and tool-result contents are preserved. Fresh prompts and requests without tool results keep their existing behavior.

This follows ggbdpq's diagnosis and d0a9ef61745d9d9900e26e7c32d05ecb7dacd303, with co-author credit. The implementation extracts complete notification blocks from otherwise filtered text, including the mid-turn user-text envelope, rather than forwarding an entire injected blob. The subsystem reference is updated.

Regression evidence: the new tests fail with the old runtime source. With the fix, task-notification, hook, mid-turn text and turn-reading test families pass together with `-race -count=5`. Eleven resume cases include system/user/developer roles, notifications in the same message as tool results, multiple notifications, both user-text/notification orders, and incomplete blocks. The bridge harness verifies delivery before the queued event releases the MCP result, and checks unchanged tool-result text.

At this exact committed head all seven acceptance checks passed with Go 1.26.8 and an isolated HOME: native/Linux/Windows vet and builds, plus `go test -tags nogui ./... -count=1 -timeout=45m` (69 packages passed). Combined branch: https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/tree/fix/issue-batch-20261023-p

The tests reuse an existing captured Claude notification fixture and synthetic envelopes. No live Claude subscription or real Claude Code 2.1.303 A/B run was performed; the original end-to-end reproduction still needs that confirmation. Cross-OS vet/builds are not native Windows/macOS runtime checks. No upstream PR opened.
@yetone 大佬推进一下进度？这个还是挺影响的..

Verified https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/commit/b7726551109dae0bc6b406cb2dddd62abd9d4e2f by cherry-picking it onto upstream/main `63be4771` and ablating the product change on Windows (Go with pinned GOPATH/GOMODCACHE/GOCACHE).

The discard surface matches the diagnosis: the drop lives only in the resume path `saidWithResults` (its single caller is the `continueWith` results handoff in `internal/gateway/claude_subscription.go`), where the system/developer skip and the `agentNotice` gate — whose injected leads hold `<task-notification>` — both removed the notification. The fix turns exactly those gates into deliverers and touches nothing else: fresh prompts and requests without results keep their ordinary path (a new protective test pins that a notification without results is not requeued), hook notices and token counts stay filtered, incomplete blocks stay filtered, and plain user text still passes. Compared to the proposed patch (a contains-and-forward branch that would also have carried hook notices when a notification shared a system message with them, and left notice-inside-a-mid-turn-envelope misattributed as user words), this version extracts complete `<task-notification>…</task-notification>` blocks — multiple blocks, both envelope orders, hooks around them — which is strictly closer to the #2060 contract; its `hooks`, `user then notice` and `notice then user` rows fail against the proposal's code.

Ablation, `go test -tags nogui -count=1 -run 'TestClaudeTaskNotificationGoesOnWithTheResults|TestClaudeTaskNoticeWithoutResultsIsNotRequeued' ./internal/gateway`, with `claude_subscription.go` reverted to `63be4771` and the tests kept:

```
--- FAIL: TestClaudeTaskNotificationGoesOnWithTheResults (0.16s)
    --- FAIL: TestClaudeTaskNotificationGoesOnWithTheResults/system (0.00s)
        claude_hook_notice_test.go:138: run was told "", want "<task-notification>\n<task-id>a964b3e6d1a85579a</task-id>\n<tool-use-id>toolu_01DHwj5uLApARZnKU3EZjxyC</tool-use-id>\n<output-file>/private/tmp/claude-501/tasks/a964b3e6d1a85579a.output</output-file>\n<status>completed</status>..."
```

8 of the 11 rows fail on base (`system`, `with results`, `user`, `developer`, `hooks`, `two notices`, `user then notice`, `notice then user`); `incomplete`, `ordinary user` and `ordinary system` stay green on base by design, pinning the preserved filters. With the fix restored, the two tests plus the neighboring hook-notice, mid-turn-user and turn-reading families (`TestClaudeHookNoticesAreNotTheUsersMessage`, `TestClaudeUsersMessageAmongHookNoticesGoesOnAlone`, `TestClaudePromptToldHookNoticesNotAsTheUsers`, `TestAgentNoticeLeavesTheUsersWords`, `TestTurnInSkipsWhatTheAgentPutIn`, `TestIntentHoldsPastWhatTheAgentPutIn`):

```
ok  	github.com/yetone/magpie/internal/gateway	3.542s
```

Attribution, checked in the commit itself: Author `vincent <webmaster@palmit.com.au>`, and the message carries exactly `Co-authored-by: ggbdpq <ggbdpq@gmail.com>`.

Drift and landing: the commit's parent (`8f931a28`) is 485 commits ahead of `63be4771`; 5 of them touch `claude_subscription.go`/`prompt.go` and shift the file by ~450 lines, but not the `saidWithResults` region — the cherry-pick applied cleanly in all three files. One landing note if both this and the earlier proposal (`d0a9ef61`) were ever applied together: both add a test named `TestClaudeTaskNotificationGoesOnWithTheResults` to `claude_hook_notice_test.go`, so one of the two has to be dropped or renamed; behaviorally this commit supersedes the proposal. Today's main (`e00fbdbb`) still lacks the fix and takes the commit's whole diff clean (`apply --3way --check`).

On reproducibility, restating what is and is not established: the reporter's A/B (2/2 `SEEN` direct, 3/3 `NOT_SEEN` through magpie, the client's own stream-json emitting the notification on both sides) stands as reported and was not re-run here or by the author, who states plainly: no live Claude subscription or real Claude Code 2.1.303 A/B was performed, the local CLI is 2.1.306, and "the original end-to-end reproduction still needs that confirmation". The tests use the captured notification fixture from #2060 plus synthetic envelopes; 2.1.303's exact bytes are inferred, not captured.

Ran here: the RED/GREEN above; `gofmt -l` clean on both files; `go vet -tags nogui ./internal/gateway` clean. Not run here: `-race` (author ran `-race -count=5` on Linux; this box has no C compiler for cgo), the 69-package acceptance sweep, and anything needing a real subscription or CLI.

Thanks for the fix, the block-extraction hardening, and the co-author credit.

Verified with AI assistance (GLM-5.3-Flash via ZCode); I've read the diff and re-ran the checks above.

*Edit* — the `-race` note above was wrong about the reason (though this round indeed didn't run it): this machine does have a C toolchain (a local mingw64, just not on the default PATH). timeline.body:
## Summary

Through the Claude subscription bridge, a background task's `<task-notification>` never reaches the model. Claude Code sends the notification with the next request — the same one that carries the finished tools' results — and the bridge hands the waiting run the results plus only what it reads as the user's words. The notification falls through two filters built for the other tail notices and is dropped, so the model answers as if no task had ended: the main session "waits forever" on a subagent that finished. Direct connections show the notification; this reproduces with masking off, so `redact` is not a factor.

## Cause

The drop is in the Claude bridge's resume path, `saidWithResults` (internal/gateway/claude_subscription.go:3257):

1. Claude Code 2.1.296+ puts the texts that trail a turn's results — hooks' notices, the `<total_tokens>` count, a mid-turn user message — into one `{role: "system"}` message after the results (captured in #2060). A background task's `<task-notification>` travels the same way; the reporter's routing log shows it: a `harness` item of notification size appears in the request's `system` part exactly when the notification is due, beside `results=[Agent, Bash]` — the system message arriving with the results.
2. When the results answer calls a run is waiting on, the bridge resumes it with `continueWith` (internal/gateway/claude_subscription.go:3366): the tool results over MCP, plus `saidWithResults` queued first as a user message (`queue`, internal/gateway/claude_subscription.go:3424).
3. `saidWithResults` skips a system message outright (`case m.Role == "system" || m.Role == "developer"`, internal/gateway/claude_subscription.go:3273 — right for hook notices, #2060) and drops texts its `agentNotice` knows (internal/gateway/claude_subscription.go:3274) — and `agentNotice`'s injected leads include `"<task-notification>"` (internal/gateway/prompt.go:655), put there for turn reading, not delivery. Either shape of the notification — the system message, or the older client's user message of its own — is filtered out. The inner model is never told.
4. Every other path tells it: a run started anew is told the whole conversation, every message rendered (renderClaudePrompt, internal/gateway/claude_subscription.go:2598; renderClaudeTurn, internal/gateway/claude_subscription.go:2886), and a relayed request passes the body as sent. Only the run kept for the results — the common case of a foreground wait, as in the reporter's probe — loses it. That matches the A/B: 2/2 `SEEN` direct, 3/3 `NOT_SEEN` through magpie, with the client's own stream-json emitting the notification on both sides.

## Fix

`saidWithResults` now tells the run a text that carries the notification: a `taskNotice` case (a contains on `<task-notification>`) ahead of the system-message and `agentNotice` cases. Hooks' notices and token counts stay out — #2060's tests are unchanged and hold. The notification is queued to the run's Claude Code as its own message, so the model hears of the finished task the way it does on a request that carries the notification alone.

## Verification

| Ablation | fix reverted → red as on base; re-applied → green; `taskNotice` forced `false` → red; restored → green | as expected, each step |
| Race | `go test -race ./internal/gateway/ -run 'TestClaudeTaskNotificationGoesOnWithTheResults|TestClaudeHookNotices|TestClaudeUsersMessageAmongHookNoticesGoesOnAlone|TestTurnInSkipsWhatTheAgentPutIn|TestIntentHoldsPastWhatTheAgentPutIn' -count=1` | ok (2.148s) |
| Format, vet | `gofmt -l` on both touched files; `go vet ./internal/gateway/` | clean |
| Build | `go build ./...` on darwin/arm64; `GOOS=linux GOARCH=amd64 go build -tags nogui ./...`; `GOOS=windows GOARCH=amd64 go build ./...` | all ok |
| Full package | `go test ./internal/gateway/ -count=1 -p 1 -timeout 30m` | ok (320.989s) |

## Not verified

- End to end with a real Claude Code 2.1.303 against a Claude subscription: 2.1.303's exact notification bytes are inferred from #2060's captured 2.1.296 shapes and the reporter's routing-log segments, not captured here. The tests cover both known shapes (the system message, and the older user message).
- The direct-connection side (no magpie) is the reporter's A/B, not re-run here.

**Red without the fix** (base `f5b01574`):

```text

FAIL

```

**Siblings**: the gates live only in the Claude bridge — no other bridge reads `saidWithResults`/`agentNotice` (rg over internal/gateway: no consumers in the Codex, OpenCode or desktop subagent paths). The fresh-run prompt path writes the text either way (guard test `TestClaudePromptToldTheTaskNotification` passes on base too); `match` takes only tool results and images, unchanged; `parseAnthropicRequest`'s block-type switch drops unknown block types on translated routes only, and the notification rides in text blocks; `prompt.go`'s `injected` list is observation and turn detection, not delivery, and is untouched.

**When the read fails**: `taskNotice` is a contains on the text part, so a malformed or absent `<task-notification>` falls through to the unchanged filters — skipped as before, no new failure path. `queue`'s timeout path is untouched: if the run's Claude Code never acknowledges the queued message, the results still go on after 2s.

**Not verified**: end to end through a real bridge with a real Claude Code 2.1.303 and a real Claude subscription; the direct-connection side of the A/B.

issue.title: edit: writing a key under a JSON array turns the array into an object and drops its entries

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
`setJSONBytes` (internal/edit/json.go:123) treats an array met on the key path as a plain value and replaces it with an object.

Reproduced on main: setting `customModels.1` on

```json
{"customModels":[{"model":"mine"}]}
```

gives `{"customModels":{"1":{…}}}`. The user's own entry is lost and the app can no longer read the field. A missing or empty array (`[]`) turns into `{"0":{…}}` the same way.

Found while reviewing magpie-community/plugins#239 (Tuanjie Cowork stores its models in `settings.json` `customModels[]`). Any agent descriptor that writes a numeric key under an array is affected.

Expected: a numeric key under an array indexes it: replacing at an index that exists, appending at `len`, refusing past it. Never turn the array into an object, and never drop an element the user wrote.

issue.title: Claude account route: tool_use is dropped, each turn ends after the first tool call (tools never executed)

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
Magpie version: magpie 0.1.1332

## Summary

When a Claude Code session is routed through a Magpie group whose served provider is the **Claude Code account** route (`provider: claude`, `kind: account`), tool calls emitted by the model are never executed and never reach the client. Each user turn produces exactly one upstream request; the client never sends the follow-up request that carries `tool_result`, so the agent appears to "stop" right after announcing a tool call.

Possibly related to #3020 (subagent completion notifications lost because Magpie rewrites requests).

## Environment

- macOS 15 (Darwin 24.6), Claude Code CLI started from a third-party terminal app (the terminal is not in the request path; `!` shell commands work normally)
- Model selected: a Magpie group with `routing: order`, first member `claude/claude-opus-5-5` (account route)
- Tools visible to the model are exposed as `mcp__magpie__*` (Bash, Read, Write, ...)

## Symptoms

1. Earlier in the same long session, tool calls worked normally (dozens of Bash/Read/Edit calls with results).
2. Mid-session, the model's context changed: the working directory became a Magpie temp dir (`.../T/magpie-claude-work-<uid>`, "not a git repository"), the system prompt became an Agent SDK prompt with `<external_system_instructions>`, and the entire prior conversation was replayed as a single `<conversation_history>` block.
3. From then on, **every** tool call failed silently, including `echo ok; date` and a `Write` to a new file. The model emits the tool call, the turn ends, and the next thing it sees is the next user message. No tool result is ever returned.
4. The tools were **not executed**: files that the `Write` calls should have created do not exist (verified with `ls` from the user's shell).
5. Restarting the Claude Code session did not fix it.

## Evidence from `~/.config/magpie/routing/<date>.jsonl`

For the affected session, after the switch, every entry is `provider=claude model=claude-opus-5-5 status=200`, one entry per user message, spaced minutes apart:

18:11:00  18:20:26  18:22:06  18:22:36  18:24:33  18:33:26  18:34:06  18:35:01  18:35:43

There is never a follow-up entry a few seconds later. In normal Claude Code operation, a `tool_use` response is always followed by another request containing `tool_result` (even when the tool errors or is unknown). Its absence means the client received a response with no `tool_use` block (i.e. treated as end of turn). So the tool call appears to be produced inside Magpie's account-route agent and dropped before reaching the client.

## Expected

Either pass `tool_use` through to the client so Claude Code executes it and continues the loop, or execute it inside the account-route agent and continue until the model ends the turn. Silently ending the turn after the first tool call should not happen.

## Notes

- Routing log entries contain `flow`, `done`, `out`, `folder`, `masked` fields; happy to provide values for entries before/after the switch if useful.
- Workaround for now: avoid the account route for this group / run Claude Code directly.

timeline.body:
这里 A/B 已经说明直连正常、经 Magpie 才丢。对于只用 Claude Code 的用户，#3933 提的「Claude Code 独占模式」可以从根上避开：Magpie 不代理、不重建上下文，只在额度到阈值时切换本地 OAuth 凭证，`<task-notification>` 这类客户端自己生成的内容原样直达 Anthropic。

当然桥接模式本身的修复仍然需要（其他客户端还要用）。

issue.title: [Feature] Claude Code 独占模式：本地切换凭证，不代理流量

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
## 背景

现在 Magpie 用代理的方式给 Claude Code 服务订阅流量：自己起 run，在路由组里静默切换账号。这样有两个问题：

1. **请求看起来不一样。** 发到 Anthropic 的请求是 Magpie 自己起的 run，不是用户本机 Claude Code 原样发出的。订阅 OAuth 凭证用在官方客户端以外的地方，正是现在风控和用户协议最在意的一点。
2. **上下文要重建。** run 复用不上的时候，整段对话会塞进第一条消息（比如 #3808 里请求被中断后的那种情况）。缓存命中率和行为都没有直连稳定。

很多用户只用 Claude Code，并不需要把订阅额度转给其他 agent。对这部分人来说，他们其实只想要 Magpie 的「额度用完自动换号」。

## 提议

新增一个 **Claude Code 独占模式**（可以和现有网关模式二选一）：

- **不监听端口，不转发流量。** Claude Code 照常直连 Anthropic，`ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` 保持不设。
- **只换本地凭证。** Magpie 保存多个账号的 OAuth 凭证（Windows/Linux 是 `~/.claude/.credentials.json`，macOS 在 Keychain，再加上 `~/.claude.json` 里的 `oauthAccount`）。某个账号的 5h/7d 窗口用到阈值时，把当前凭证换成下一个账号的。
- **复用 Magpie 已有的东西**：账号列表、额度查询、路由组的优先级和策略，只是把「切换」的落点从上游请求换成本地凭证文件。

## 可以参考的实现

[realiti4/claude-swap](https://github.com/realiti4/claude-swap) 已经验证了这条路可行：

- 写凭证时拿着 Claude Code 自己的凭证锁，避免和它的 token 刷新撞车。
- Windows/Linux 上 Claude Code 每条消息都会重读凭证文件，切换在下一条消息生效；macOS 的 Keychain 缓存大约 30 秒。
- 自动切换有阈值（默认 90%）、冷却时间和回差，防止来回切。切换前先刷新目标账号的 token，refresh token 失效的账号会被隔离。
- 只换账号相关的凭证，MCP 等与账号无关的 OAuth 状态保持不动。
- 注意不要先 `/logout`，否则可能把要离开的那个账号的 refresh token 吊销掉。

## 好处

- 对 Anthropic 来说，流量就是官方 Claude Code 客户端发的，没有中间层改写。
- 不用重建上下文，prompt cache 的行为和直连一样。
- Magpie 挂掉也不影响 Claude Code 正常使用，最多是不再自动换号。

## 不在范围内

- 不给其他 agent/客户端供应订阅额度（那部分仍然由现有网关模式负责）。
- 不改变现有网关模式的行为。

To check that it covers skygunner's cases, I adapted the 11 resume rows from https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/commit/b7726551109dae0bc6b406cb2dddd62abd9d4e2f to main's test names (system, developer, user, with results, hooks, two notices, user then notice, notice then user, incomplete, ordinary user, ordinary system). All 11 pass on current main, and the 8 the fork's commit says fail on the old code are red at `9a2106220^`. Nothing in the fork's diff is missing from main, so I didn't port it.

Thanks to ggbdpq for the diagnosis and to skygunner for the cases.

issue.title: Claude bridge: the model gets system-reminder fragments instead of my prompt

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
**Problem:** With the `claude` (subscription) member, the model doesn't receive my prompt. It receives pieces of the system-reminders instead. The gateway log shows it parsed my prompt fine.

**Expected:** the model answers my prompt.

**Actual:** After `/clear` I sent one long prompt. The model replied: "Your message came through as fragments of configuration text (memory-file instructions and a skill list) with no actual request in it." When I asked what it saw, it listed the user-email system-reminder, a memory-instructions block that started mid-sentence, a hooks/status-line fragment, two skill descriptions and the date. None of my prompt was in the list.

**Log:** Four requests, 11:57:50–11:58:37, all 200 with `tries[0].id: "claude"`. The first request's `prompt` parse is 70,906 tokens with one chat turn of 770 tokens, so the gateway received my prompt. The log has no bodies, so I can't see what the inner `claude` was given.

**Setup:** Magpie 0.1.2689, Windows, Claude Code 2.1.316. Group `auto-claude-sonnet-5-5` = `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5`, then `claude/claude-sonnet-5-5`.

**Related:** #4407, #3020 and #2060 look like the same area, but they are tool-result turns. This one is the first turn after `/clear`.

**Not tried:** `claudePrintMode: true`, or pinning the group to the `claude` member.
